intelligence.title: Not Reproducible Is Never "Cannot Appear"

intelligence.human_view: This is the difference between an absence of evidence and evidence of absence, stated as a working law. A probe runs in an environment; when that environment cannot reach the thing being probed — the VM cannot reach Supabase — the probe's silence says nothing about the live system. It says something about the probe. The reconciliation probe wrote "cannot appear" because it could not find the banner element in its own blind environment, and the verdict carried that claim as if it were a fact about the Dashboard. Then Shawn's screenshot showed the banner, real, on the staged page — and the whole verdict had to be corrected in writing. The numbers really did disagree: 1466 on the tiles, 466 in the dial center, 350 on the spine. The correction is the honorable part: the captain named the miss, owned it ("captain owns the miss"), corrected the verdict file, and dispatched a fresh diagnosis. But the lesson is preventive, not corrective: a probe must state its own blindness before it states any conclusion. "I could not reproduce this in the VM" is a complete and honest sentence. "It cannot appear" is a claim about the world that a blind probe has no right to make — and when it is wrong, it is wrong in exactly the direction that hides a real defect from the person who needs to see it.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine you close your eyes and say "there's no cookie in the kitchen!" — but you didn't even LOOK! You can't say something isn't there just because YOU couldn't see it! If your eyes are closed, you say "I couldn't see it" — not "it's not there!" Shawn's picture PROVED the banner was really there!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like saying there's no rain because you're sitting inside with the curtains shut, love. You didn't look out the window! If you can't see it, you say "I couldn't see it" — you don't say "it isn't there." The picture proved it was there all along, and saying so honestly is what makes it right.
intelligence.naya_view: I never say "cannot appear" from a probe that could not see. When my environment cannot reach the live data, I say so plainly: not reproducible in the VM. I do not certify absence from blindness. If a claim in a verdict is wrong, I correct it in writing, I own the miss, and I dispatch the fresh diagnosis. The banner is real until proven otherwise by a probe that can actually see it.
